newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo sees 100 bln yen 1996/97 current profit.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo sees 100 bln yen 1996/97 current profit.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said on Friday that it expects to post a parent current profit of around 100 billion yen in the year to March 31, if the dollar stays at around 123 yen.
The company also said in a statement that it expects its business to perform steadily in 1997/98 if the dollar were at around 120 yen.
Nintendo said it would cut the domestic price of its 64-bit game machine, Nintendo 64, to 16,800 yen from 25,000 yen from March 14, 1997.
It will be able to reduce the price as it plans to boost production in two phases, a company spokesman said.
It will increase monthly production of its flagship game console to 800,000 units in April from the current 700,000 and then to one million in May, he said.

Nintendo also said it would launch a new game title, "Star Fox 64", in Japan in April. Concurrently, it would start selling "jolting pak", a device which vibrates the control pad in accordance with movements in the game, in Japan.
The new products may be launched on the U.S. market within one or two months of their apearance in Japan, but no definite date has been set, the spokesman said.

As of the end of last year, the company had sold a total of 3.99 million units of Nintendo 64 in Japan and the United States, the statement said. The game machine is scheduled to be launched in Europe on March 1, it said.
